texts.orig: Q: What exactly is the job of a product manager?
texts.text: Q: What exactly is the job of a product manager?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: I generally avoid meta questions like this, since they’re rarely actionable or useful. But because this is such a common PM interview question and because I’ve gotten this question from readers enough times and never found a definition that I like elsewhere, I’m going to tackle it this week.

texts.orig: The job of a product manager
texts.text: The job of a product manager

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Your job as a PM is to deliver business impact by marshaling the resources of your team to identify and solve the most impactful customer problems.
texts.text: Your job as a PM is to deliver business impact by marshaling the resources of your team to identify and solve the most impactful customer problems.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: There are three parts to this, each essential:
texts.text: There are three parts to this, each essential:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Fundamentally, you are responsible for delivering business impact. If your team drives positive impact—hitting important goals, reducing costs, shipping an important project, etc.—you’re doing your job.
texts.text: Fundamentally, you are responsible for delivering business impact. If your team drives positive impact—hitting important goals, reducing costs, shipping an important project, etc.—you’re doing your job.

texts.orig: How the PM role varies by company
texts.text: How the PM role varies by company

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Everything we’ve talked about above is based on the typical PM role. But the PM role is rarely typical. If you’re looking to get into PM, it’s important that you look into how the company you work at (or plan to work at) specifically looks at the PM role. There are two axes across which the PM role most varies:
texts.text: Everything we’ve talked about above is based on the typical PM role. But the PM role is rarely typical. If you’re looking to get into PM, it’s important that you look into how the company you work at (or plan to work at) specifically looks at the PM role. There are two axes across which the PM role most varies:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In the end, no matter how many definitions and details you read about the PM role, it’ll never be exactly the same at any company. Every founder and product leader will have their own unique take on what they expect from their PMs. So what to do?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: If you’re already at a company and looking to understand the role better, ask your manager what “amazing” in the role would look like.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: If you’re exploring getting into PM, ask the companies you talk to (1) what skills they care about most and (2) how much say a PM has compared to other functions.
